name: Lafayette Textiles Corp
old_description: For over 35 years Lafayette has remained at the forefront of innovation, constantly developing new styles of fabrics all year round.
about:
Lafayette Textiles Corp operates from Vernon, California, where it has been developing knit fabrics for over 35 years. President Sean Zahedi leads the company, which began as an innovator in textile design and now runs a fully integrated domestic production facility.

The company knits, dyes, and finishes its own fabrics on circular knitting machines ranging from 4‑cut to 28‑cut gauge. Its capabilities cover jersey, French terry, fleece, loop terry, interlock, rib, thermal, pique, ponte de roma, and diagonal French terry constructions, with a focus on sustainable fibers such as organic cotton, recycled cotton, and bamboo blends. Production minimums typically run 500–1,000 yards per color and construction.

Lafayette serves the apparel industry, supplying brands and designers who need quick‑turn domestic knits. Its fabrics have been used for merchandise by acts such as Rufus Du Sol, and the company maintains a New York contact for East Coast clients.

Zahedi has emphasized a two‑pronged sustainability approach: producing eco‑friendly fabrics while reducing water use in dyeing and finishing. The firm highlights its made‑in‑USA supply chain, dedicated machines that prevent fiber contamination, and lead times of two to four weeks as key differentiators.

name: Lake Michigan Wire
old_description: Lake Michigan Wire manufactures knurled pins, straightened and cut wire, and large diameter wire forms to make whatever project you are working on a success.
about:
Lake Michigan Wire, LLC operates from Holland, Michigan, where it has been in business for over 30 years. The company is part of the Agritek Family of Companies and specializes in fabricated wire products.

The company manufactures knurled pins, straightened and cut wire, and large-diameter wire forms and assemblies. Lake Michigan Wire handles orders ranging from 100 pieces to hundreds of thousands, emphasizing quick turnaround and custom packaging.

Lake Michigan Wire serves the automotive, electrical, farm and garden, hobby and toy, office furniture, and medical industries, as well as customers requiring plastic injection/insert molding and metal stamping components. Examples include seat belt assembly safety components for automotive, wire products for electrical applications, cut wire and welded assemblies for agricultural use, and pins for hobby and toy products.

The company emphasizes tackling difficult projects that competitors decline, controlling the manufacturing process, and standing behind its services. It highlights a commitment to employee training, selective supplier sourcing, and well-maintained custom equipment to ensure efficiency and repeatability, along with worldwide shipping experience.

name: Lake Shore Electric Corporation
old_description: Specializes in sheet metal, copper, and stainless-steel fabrication
about:
Lake Shore Electric Corporation was founded in Cleveland, Ohio, in 1922 and today operates from its headquarters in Bedford, Ohio. The company is organized as a limited liability company (Lake Shore Electric, LLC) and has spent more than a century developing power distribution equipment for industrial, utility, and data-center customers.

The firm designs, fabricates, and assembles commercial and industrial electrical equipment entirely in-house, a vertically integrated model that covers sheet metal, copper, and stainless-steel fabrication through final assembly and testing. Its six product lines — Enclosure, Distribute, eHOUSE, Control, Connect, and Transfer — include switchgear, transfer switches, prefabricated electrical buildings (e-houses), and custom enclosures built to project specifications. Design-build capabilities allow the engineering team to work from concept through commissioning, and the component-agnostic approach avoids vendor lock-in.

Lake Shore Electric serves data centers, utilities, industrial manufacturing plants, oil and gas operations, mining sites, wastewater treatment facilities, and commercial buildings. Recent projects include UL 891 switchboards for utility-scale battery energy storage systems, a custom EV charging switchboard for Greenlane Infrastructure in California, and prefabricated electrical equipment houses for customers facing year-long lead times elsewhere.

The company emphasizes its U.S.-based fabrication, fast turnaround times, and compliance with Build America, Buy America (BABA) requirements as key differentiators. A track record of more than 50 years manufacturing UL-listed products, combined with in-house testing before shipment, underpins its focus on reliability and reduced downtime for mission-critical installations.

name: Lansdale Semiconductor Inc
old_description: Lansdale Semiconductor still manufactures some of the most popular…and timeless commercial wireless, telecommunications, military and aerospace integrated circuits (IC’s) classic designs.
about:
Lansdale Semiconductor Inc. operates from Phoenix, Arizona, where it has spent more than four decades producing mission-critical, high-reliability semiconductors for military and commercial markets. The company is led by President R. Dale Lillard, who has overseen its expansion into aftermarket manufacturing of classic integrated circuits.

The firm manufactures over 3,000 classic IC designs in their original packages, replicating parts originally produced by AMD, Fairchild, Freescale, Harris, Intel, Motorola, National, Philips (Signetics), and Raytheon. Its semiconductor aftermarket program covers life-cycle management, JAN- and SMD-qualified devices, and RoHS/REACH-compliant production, allowing customers to avoid redesigns of legacy systems.

Lansdale serves aerospace and defense, commercial wireless, and telecommunications sectors. Its components support legacy military platforms and commercial infrastructure, with Raytheon having awarded the company a Four-Star Excellence rating. The company also maintains a network of distribution partners for global reach.

The business was built on the premise that obsolescence should not force a redesign. By continuing to fabricate exact replicas of discontinued ICs, Lansdale provides a continuous, cost-effective supply for systems where substitution is not an option, and it actively combats counterfeit parts in the supply chain.

old_description: FREE SHIPPING | Order today for free U.S. shipping on all Larson storm doors.
about:
Based in Brookings, South Dakota, Larson Manufacturing produces storm doors, retractable screens, and replacement parts for residential entryways. The company does not publicly disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or founder names.

The product line includes the Maximum View storm door series with interchangeable glass and screen panels, retractable screens for doors, windows, and patios, and a range of replacement components such as sweeps, handlesets, and magnetic closers. Manufacturing processes, facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not specified.

Larson serves homeowners directly through its e‑commerce site and retail channels, while also supporting a network of dealers and installation professionals via a dedicated Pro Center program. Its products are used in residential construction, remodeling, and home‑improvement projects.

The company highlights its SureLatch™ magnetic locking technology, which provides an audible click to confirm secure closure, and the Maximum View door design that maximizes natural light. Additional differentiators cited include free U.S. shipping on all storm door orders, expert‑tested installation guides, comprehensive warranties, and a brand portfolio representing over 200 combined years of material‑science expertise.

name: Laser Metal Fabrication
old_description: Serving contractors, manufacturers, and engineering teams with high-precision cutting, fast turnaround, and custom fabrication solutions.
about:
Laser Metal Fabrication operates from Twin Falls, Idaho, in the Magic Valley region. The company was founded by Cort Johnson, who holds a bachelor's degree in Welding Fabrication Technology from Brigham Young University–Idaho and a master's in Project Management from Idaho State University. Johnson has lived in Twin Falls for nine years with his family, and his technical expertise and local roots form the basis of the business.

The shop provides precision laser cutting of sheet, plate, and tube — handling material from 24 gauge through 1-inch plate on sheets up to 6 by 12 feet, and tube up to 8 inches by 21 feet. CNC bending covers sheet metal up to 11 feet and tubing up to 24 feet with a 2.5 mm tolerance, supported by a 150-ton, 10-foot press brake. Welding capabilities include SMAW, MIG, TIG, and laser welding, complemented by fully integrated assembly services and 3D modeling and design. The facility runs documented production workflows to support scalable production for both industrial and ornamental applications.

Laser Metal Fabrication serves contractors, manufacturers, and engineering teams across industrial, commercial, and private projects. The company also produces custom home products such as window well covers and vent covers for residential and commercial clients. Its regional footprint spans the Intermountain West, with service areas including Twin Falls, Jerome, Buhl, Burley, and the broader Magic Valley, while nationwide shipping is available for production parts.

The company positions itself as a partner rather than a vendor, emphasizing documented processes for repeatability and quality control from one-off prototypes to full production runs. Its instant CAD estimator allows customers to upload DXF, DWG, STL, STEP, or IGES files for review-ready estimates, and the shop handles secondary services — forming, welding, and assembly — under one roof.

name: Lattice Semiconductor Corporation
old_description: Creates Industry’s Leading Secure Management and Control Platform
about:
Lattice Semiconductor Corporation was founded in 1983 in Hillsboro, Oregon, within the region known as the Silicon Forest. The company began as a developer of programmable logic devices and has grown into a global supplier of low-power field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and related software tools. It operates as a publicly traded corporation.

The company designs and develops FPGA silicon platforms — including the Nexus family for ultra-low-power small FPGAs, the Avant family for mid-range FPGAs, and the long-standing MachXO platform — along with IP cores optimized for AI, security, and connectivity. It provides design software such as Lattice Radiant and Lattice Propel, and solution stacks (Sentry for platform firmware resilience, mVision for embedded vision, sensAI for machine learning) that accelerate customer development. Lattice also offers custom design services, programming services, and, through its AMI acquisition, platform firmware (Aptio, MegaRAC, Tektagon), middleware, and datacenter orchestration solutions. The company reports the largest installed base of small FPGAs worldwide and serves tens of thousands of customers globally.

Lattice’s products are used across compute, communications, industrial, automotive, aerospace and defense, and consumer markets. Specific applications include datacenter infrastructure and AI acceleration, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), motor control, robotics, embedded vision, and edge AI inference. The AMI firmware portfolio is embedded across thousands of datacenter platforms, serving the server and storage ecosystem.

Lattice emphasizes its position as the low-power programmable leader, citing its #1 ranking in small FPGA supply, 20-plus-year product longevity commitments, and the combination of FPGA hardware with AMI’s firmware stack to deliver what it calls the industry’s most complete secure management and control platform. The company highlights flexible silicon platforms, a comprehensive software and IP ecosystem, and long-term support as key differentiators.

name: Lcl Electronics
old_description: As a leading provider of electronic manufacturing services, LCL Electronics demonstrates expertise in temperature testing according to MIL-STD-810, Methods 501, 502, and 503.
about:
LCL Electronics is based in Baxter, Minnesota. The company is a HUBZone-certified small business that primarily serves the U.S. Department of Defense and all five branches of the U.S. Armed Forces. It holds a CAGE code of 2Y430 and is ITAR registered.

The company provides electronic manufacturing and assembly services, including surface mount technology, wave and reflow soldering, cable and wiring harness assembly, conformal coating, encapsulation potting, and mechanical assembly. It also offers advanced testing capabilities such as temperature, humidity, vibration, and shock testing per MIL-STD-810, as well as X-ray inspection, in-circuit testing, environmental stress screening, and first article testing. Engineering support includes test equipment design and mechanical development using SolidWorks 3D CAD.

LCL Electronics works with defense and aerospace customers, including the U.S. Department of Defense, all five military branches, and Lockheed Martin as an approved supplier. Its NAICS classifications cover relay and industrial control manufacturing and printed circuit assembly.

The firm differentiates itself through its certifications—ISO 9001:2015, AS9100D, ITAR registration, and HUBZone status—and its focus on compliance with military standards such as MIL-STD-810.

name: Lear Corporation
old_description: Manufactures automotive wiring harnesses and electrical distribution systems.
about:
Lear Corporation is headquartered in Southfield, Michigan, and traces its origins to 1917. The company has grown over more than a century to become the largest U.S.-based automotive supplier.

Lear designs and manufactures automotive seating systems and electrical distribution (E-Systems) products, including wiring harnesses, terminals, and connectors. With a global workforce of approximately 164,300 employees, the company operates numerous manufacturing and engineering centers worldwide.

Lear serves the global automotive industry, supplying seating and electrical systems to major vehicle manufacturers. The company’s customer base includes Ford, which recognized Lear as a 2026 Supplier of the Year for Sustainability, among other OEMs.

Lear emphasizes innovation and sustainability as core differentiators, highlighted by its FlexAir™ sustainable seating technology and a corporate commitment to reducing environmental impact, as stated by President and CEO Ray Scott.

name: Lee Andersen Art Clothing
old_description: After more than 35 years Lee Andersen is stepping down from designing and we are shutting down our website for sales.
about:
The company was built around Andersen’s personal design practice, which began in New Zealand and continued after she relocated to the United States. No formal founding year or ownership structure is disclosed in public materials.

The studio produced handmade women’s apparel, with Andersen creating over 6,000 individual garments during her career. Pieces were constructed in the company’s Maryland facility and sold through its website and a physical outlet store in the Long Reach Village Shopping Center. The operation also housed a makerspace where emerging designers could work under Andersen’s guidance.

The brand’s clientele included high-profile wearers such as the Queen of Spain, actress Phylicia Rashad on “The Cosby Show,” and author Diana Gabaldon. Beyond direct-to-consumer sales, the company transitioned in its final phase to education, with Andersen teaching sewing and pattern-making through the MD Fashion Institute and Howard Community College.

Andersen positioned the label on its American-made, handcrafted approach and the depth of its design archive. The decision to cease commercial production was framed as a personal retirement rather than a business failure, with the website repurposed as an archival resource for authenticating past pieces.
